title: Choose the visual world for Navya Ed Tech
question: The roll assigned Snap Lab. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. (Primary visitor: parents choosing coding classes for kids aged 8 to 16.)

options.label: Snap Lab
options.lineage: the snap-together code blocks every young coder starts with
options.thesis: The whole site is built like a program a child snaps together: every section is a block that clicks into the next, and the blocks turn into real Python as the child grows.
materials: chunky rounded blocks with notches and tabs
options.viewport: Headline set beside a live block stack (when green flag clicked, move, say, repeat) that sits over the same program written in Python; a hat-shaped orange 'Book a free trial class' block is the primary action.
options.risk: Can tip into childish for teen and adult learners if every surface performs; blocks must stay structural, and the shapes must be our own, never a copy of Scratch's branding.

raised.raise: One idea per viewport: each block stack gets generous empty space around it, never a crowded wall of cards.
Connections draw in sequence: blocks snap on one after another as they enter, never all at once.
State lives on the block itself: open, starting soon and full change the block's own colour and tab, not a separate badge.
Curriculum notes are pinned to blocks on leader lines, so a parent reads what each step teaches exactly where it sits.
One depth scale: rest, hover and pressed are three fixed elevation steps used on every interactive element.

options.label: Build Manual
options.thesis: Every course is a numbered build plan, so parents see exactly what their child assembles, class by class.
options.viewport: A booklet cover (ages, course name, parts list: classes, kids, mentor, projects) facing a four-panel step spread.
options.risk: The most familiar of the strong options; it also needs a set of custom isometric drawings we would have to create.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Admissions as a station board: every batch is a departure with ages, start day, time and seat status.
options.viewport: A live board of upcoming batches whose characters cascade into place, with 'Reserve a seat' as the action.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: batches, schedules and seat status map to rows and win on product clarity; loses on warmth for parents of young children.
options.risk: Cold for an 8-year-old's parent, and it only works when the admin keeps real batch times up to date.

options.label: Fashion Flagship
options.thesis: Monumental type and slow full-bleed imagery.
options.viewport: One enormous word over a single full-bleed photo.
options.risk: Needs real photography we do not have.
options.case: Fuses poorly: parents need clarity and warmth, and there is no real photography to carry it.

options.label: Wildstyle Blackbook
options.thesis: Interlocking marker letterforms as the whole map.
options.viewport: The name knitted into one letter mass with arrows.
options.case: Fuses poorly: legibility and trust lose to style.

options.label: Chromatophore Skin
options.thesis: A living surface whose pattern is the state.
options.viewport: A patterned living field reacting to the cursor.
options.risk: Heavy GPU work on low-end phones.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to parents or coding classes.
options.kept: State drawn on the surface itself.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Rods and cords whose forces are the interface.
options.viewport: A breathing column annotated with force values.
options.case: Fuses poorly: engineering abstraction, not a child's learning.
options.kept: Annotations pinned to nodes on leader lines.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Bitmap type drifting over a black void by depth.
options.viewport: One still line of ivory text over drifting dust.
options.risk: Reads as a hacker scene to parents.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dark and cryptic for a family audience.
options.kept: One shared depth scale for every state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A friendly kids-coding school site, done cleanly: bright blue, soft illustration, headline left and visual right, feature cards below.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and trial-class button beside an illustrated panel with floating feature cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other coding school by design.
